h1: Is Danelfin Worth It for Your Stock Research?
subtitle: A practical breakdown of Danelfin AI Score mechanics, published backtests, subscription costs, and ideal trading styles.
introText:
[Danelfin](https://danelfin.com) is worth paying for if you trade individual equities on multi-month time horizons and want transparent research, but it is not worth the cost for day traders or passive index fund investors. At ModernWallet, we review stock research software by weighing core algorithmic models against retail investor needs and realistic market tradeoffs. In our evaluation of the [best AI stock pickers](/roundup/best-ai-stock-pickers/), Danelfin earned our recommendation for most retail investors because it combines an artificial intelligence (AI) predictive rating model with full factor transparency instead of hiding behind an opaque algorithm.

Danelfin evaluates thousands of daily data points across United States and European equities to assign each asset an AI Score from 1 to 10. While Danelfin's published backtests show that top-rated stocks outperformed broader market benchmarks over three-month windows, retail investors must weigh those claims against subscription fees and execution requirements. Understanding how [AI stock trading mechanics](/guides/ai-stock-trading-explained/) operate helps determine whether a Danelfin subscription justifies its monthly cost for your investment portfolio.

sections.heading: What the Danelfin AI Score Actually Measures
sections.body:
Danelfin calculates an overall AI Score from 1 to 10 by analyzing technical indicators, fundamental valuation metrics, sentiment data, and low-risk signals for each stock. Danelfin evaluates thousands of daily data points across United States and European equities to generate this rating. A score of 10 indicates the highest statistical probability of outperforming the broader market over a three-month horizon. In contrast, a score of 1 indicates expected market underperformance across that same three-month predictive window.

The primary structural advantage of Danelfin is its explainable architecture. Rather than operating as an opaque black box, Danelfin breaks down every overall score into distinct sub-scores for technical indicators, fundamental valuation metrics, market sentiment data, and low-risk signals. This breakdown shows investors the specific metrics driving a numerical rating, enabling informed personal choices before executing orders through an outside brokerage.

sections.heading: Published Backtest Performance and Regulatory Realities
sections.body:
Danelfin's published backtest demonstrates that stocks receiving an AI Score of 10 outperformed the market since 2017, while stocks rated 1 underperformed. Historical data published by Danelfin tracks the multi-month trajectory of equities categorized by their assigned predictive score. Across these historical models, top-rated assets generated higher returns relative to broader market benchmarks, while bottom-tier assets lagged behind the market average. This backtested spread reflects the statistical framework of the three-month predictive horizon.

However, historical backtests cannot guarantee future investment performance. Both the [Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2024-36) and the [Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA)](https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/artificial-intelligence-and-investment-fraud) have warned investors that algorithmic models do not ensure market-beating returns. Automated outputs should never be treated as guaranteed profit signals, and retail investors must manage portfolio risks independently.

sections.heading: Subscription Costs across Free and Paid Tiers
sections.body:
Danelfin provides a free tier with limited stock reports alongside paid Plus and Pro subscription plans. The free tier lets prospective users examine limited stock reports to evaluate the Danelfin interface before committing capital. For expanded access, paid tiers unlock more extensive data and tracking tools. The Plus plan costs approximately $22 per month, while the Pro plan costs approximately $59 per month.

Because subscription pricing and specific feature bundles can shift over time, verify current rates directly on the [Danelfin](https://danelfin.com) pricing page before subscribing. Danelfin does not publicly publish an independently confirmed refund policy, cancellation terms, or mobile app specifications. Review those subscription details on the [Danelfin](https://danelfin.com) website prior to entering payment information.

sections.heading: Investors Who Get the Most Value from Danelfin
sections.body:
Danelfin delivers the most value to retail swing traders who hold individual equities for several months and value transparent quantitative research. Investors holding stocks over multi-month periods benefit directly from Danelfin's three-month predictive horizon. Because Danelfin is a stock research and scoring service rather than an automated trade-execution program, investors retain full discretion over their portfolios. You review the explainable sub-scores on your own schedule and place trades manually through your selected brokerage.

Danelfin provides structured technical, fundamental, and sentiment data points without forcing automated trades. To see how Danelfin compares against rival services, read our [best AI stock pickers roundup](/roundup/best-ai-stock-pickers/).

sections.heading: Who Should Skip Danelfin for Other Approaches
sections.body:
Day traders seeking split-second execution and passive index investors should skip Danelfin entirely. Day traders who rely on rapid intraday scalping cannot use Danelfin effectively. Danelfin's three-month predictive window does not produce real-time, second-by-second trade alerts. High-frequency day traders requiring intraday execution signals should evaluate specialized alternatives such as Trade Ideas in our guide to the [best AI trading bots](/roundup/best-ai-trading-bots/).

Passive long-term index investors should also avoid Danelfin and similar stock-scoring services. Chasing individual stock momentum introduces unnecessary volatility, whereas systematically purchasing low-cost total-market index funds is mathematically superior for passive wealth accumulation. Additionally, anyone seeking guaranteed investment profits should pass on Danelfin, as algorithmic predictions carry inherent market risk.

faqItems.question: Is Danelfin worth it?
faqItems.answer: Danelfin is worth the subscription cost for swing traders who hold stocks over multi-month periods and want transparent, factor-based research. It is not worth it for day traders who need intraday execution signals or passive investors who rely on index funds. Subscribers gain access to clear 1-to-10 stock ratings supported by technical, fundamental, and sentiment sub-scores.

faqItems.question: Is Danelfin legit?
faqItems.answer: Yes, Danelfin is a legitimate stock research service that scores thousands of United States and European equities using measurable market data. Danelfin publishes transparent sub-scores across fundamentals, technical indicators, sentiment, and risk signals rather than acting as an opaque black box. However, regulatory bodies like the SEC and FINRA caution that no algorithmic system guarantees profitable returns.

faqItems.question: How much does Danelfin cost?
faqItems.answer: Danelfin offers a free plan alongside two primary paid subscription tiers. The Plus plan costs approximately $22 per month, while the Pro plan costs approximately $59 per month. Users should verify current pricing and plan features directly on the [Danelfin](https://danelfin.com) website before subscribing.

faqItems.question: How accurate is Danelfin?
faqItems.answer: Danelfin's internal backtests indicate that stocks awarded a top score of 10 outperformed the market since 2017, while stocks rated 1 underperformed. However, Danelfin does not publish a confirmed overall win-rate percentage, and past backtested results do not guarantee future investment returns. Investors must place their own trades manually and manage execution risk independently.

faqItems.question: Is there a free version of Danelfin?
faqItems.answer: Yes, Danelfin provides a free tier that gives users access to limited stock reports and scoring data. This tier allows investors to test the Danelfin interface and rating structure before committing to a paid plan. Upgrading to the Plus or Pro tier unlocks expanded reports and stock tracking capabilities.
